newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends defensive on renewed scare.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends defensive on renewed scare.

text.p: The Philippine peso remained defensive on Wednesday as the market was unnerved by renewed fears of a devaluation, traders said.
The Singapore Strait Times in its Wednesday edition quoted Trade and Industry Secretary Cesar Bautista as saying the devaluation of the peso would be discussed at today's Monetary Board meeting.
"It was a bloodbath," a trader said.
The Central Bank may have unloaded $630 million to $645 million to calm the jittery market, traders estimated.
The Central Bank was selling at 26.40 pesos for next-day settlement and at 26.418 for Friday-delivery, traders said.
The peso ended unchanged at 26.40 to the dollar but managed to strengthen to 26.398 in the afternoon.
Volume was at a hefty $1.017 billion, near the record $1.049 billion posted last week when the Central Bank was forced to defend the peso after the de facto devaluation of the Thai baht.
President Fidel Ramos, in response to a question at his weekly news conference, said there was a deliberate attempt to undermine the peso.
"The Central Bank was really out there to defend the peso," one trader said, noting that the Central Bank also stood firm on its 30 percent overnight rate to discourage speculation.
The peso had been attacked in recent months due to the spillover effects of Thailand's financial problems.
